stem:
Sneha compares how fast equal amounts of water dry. She uses a shallow wide plate and a narrow-necked bottle. She can also change temperature and how humid the air is. She asks whether water must boil before it can evaporate.

Which prediction is correct?

options.text: With the same amount, temperature, and humidity, water in the shallow wide plate evaporates faster than in the narrow-necked bottle.
The wide plate always finishes first, even if it holds much more water.
With temperature and exposed area equal, water evaporates faster in humid air than in dry air.
Water near room temperature cannot evaporate at all until it boils.

teacher.key_rationale: More exposed area speeds evaporation. Humidity slows it. Liquid water can evaporate below boiling.
